summary: The prisma mcp server no longer exposes a migrate-reset tool; an agent must run prisma migrate reset through the CLI (where the AI safety checkpoint applies) instead.

prisma db push --accept-data-loss now goes through the AI safety checkpoint and refuses to run under a detected AI agent without explicit user consent (PRISMA_USER_CONSENT_FOR_DANGEROUS_AI_ACTION); before, only --force-reset, db drop and migrate reset were guarded.

The AI safety checkpoint detects many more agents (Codex CLI on Linux, Qwen Code, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Cline, Goose, Amp, Crush, Augment, Antigravity, Replit Agent, Devin, and generic AI_AGENT/AGENT variables), so destructive commands now refuse in environments that used to pass.
prisma init now installs the prisma/skills agent-skill catalog into the new project by default (opt out with --no-skills), where it used to scaffold only the schema, config and .env.
On Windows, engine binaries are cached in a user-level %APPDATA%\Prisma directory instead of the cwd-relative node_modules\.cache.
Prisma Studio's SQL execution, linting and navigation resolve unqualified identifiers against the schema selected in Studio instead of always the adapter's default schema.

Without --config, the Prisma 7 CLI looks first for root prisma7.config.* files, then .config/prisma7.*, and only then falls back to prisma.config.*; a prisma7.config.* that fails to load is reported instead of falling back.
prisma init in new projects writes prisma7.config.ts instead of prisma.config.ts.
Prisma Studio's local server binds to 127.0.0.1 instead of all interfaces, rejects browser requests from origins other than its own localhost URL, and stops sending wildcard CORS headers.
prisma generate may now show a one-time interactive prompt offering to install Prisma's agent skills (skipped in CI, containers, hooks, lifecycle scripts, watch mode and with --no-hints).
A globally installed prisma CLI now warns during prisma generate when its version differs from the project's local prisma or @prisma/client.
The AI safety checkpoint also covers interactive prisma db push data-loss confirmations, not only runs with --accept-data-loss.

A statement that Prisma Client splits into several chunks (too many bind values, e.g. a large deleteMany or read) now runs inside a transaction and is rolled back if a later chunk fails, where earlier chunks used to stay committed.
An invalid Date passed to $queryRaw/$executeRaw throws PrismaClientValidationError instead of a generic error.

Bytes values returned by queries and raw queries are Uint8Arrays that own a standalone ArrayBuffer, instead of views into Node's shared Buffer pool (whose .buffer exposed unrelated bytes and an 8192 byteLength).
